operator_signal: Kevin's wave-6 imageheavy-open record's named follow-up (record 20260929-035000): 'the many-file roster scan' — the roster fold's cold-scan cost on the many-sessions class. The measured baseline (pre-#3098): the fold ~10.4ms per cold scan on the 22.9MB real-session fixture (~1.8ms the image share). The open question: the cost per cold scan vs SESSION COUNT (the current shape re-scans per cold open; the cost class on a many-session box was the unmeasured part).
hypothesis: The cold roster scan (session_scan::list_sessions: per-file bounded header gate + the whole-file fold building the SessionInfo row) scales ~linearly with TOTAL SESSION BYTES: the fold is byte-driven (~0.45ms/MB at the imageheavy unit) and the scan re-folds EVERY file per cold process (the scan-state cache is process-local, matching TS). Prediction: N real-size sessions cost ~N x 10ms per fresh-daemon first catalog touch; the wall crosses the user-noticeable class at tens of sessions and seconds at hundreds. Secondary prediction (the warm path the imageheavy record did not probe at scale): the scan-state cache's retained-usage-entry budget (SESSION_SCAN_MAX_RETAINED_USAGE_ENTRIES = 400_000, the TS-ported constant) plus the cyclic per-scan walk can thrash 100% once a box's TOTAL retained usage entries exceed the budget — turning EVERY scan (warm or cold) into a full re-fold for the process's lifetime.
approach: MEASUREMENT ONLY (no product change; the probe tree never ships). (1) TS-PARITY ANALYSIS FIRST (the brief's leg 2): the TS roster build path mapped end-to-end before any measurement — daemon-supervisor.ts handleSavedSessionList (line 3170) -> this.catalog.list -> DaemonCatalogClient (daemon-catalog-process.ts: a dedicated long-lived child process per daemon, IPC list/resolve, dies with the daemon on disconnect line 142) -> SessionManager.list/listAll (session-manager.ts:2786/2806) -> listSessionsFromDir (1698: readdir + .jsonl filter + per-file readSessionInfo, streams onSession/onProgress, sorts by modified at the END) -> scanSessionInfo (~1410: stat; unchanged -> the in-memory sessionScanStates Map hit [storeSessionScanState re-stores, line 1378-1387, the LRU by Map insertion order + the retainedUsageEntries budget]; grown + scannedPrefixIntact -> the resumed fold from state.offset; rewritten -> whole fold; the post-scan re-stat + inode re-check + retryOnReplacement). NO on-disk index, NO cross-boot persistence anywhere in the TS session-manager (grep: no writeFileSync/index/cache artifacts beyond the session files themselves; TS's own design comment: 'Keep large families (~2k sessions, 150k usage entries) and growth headroom resident'). The port mirrors the shape (session_scan.rs + session_store/info.rs: the LRU BTreeMap cache, the 16-byte resume tail, the bounded header gate, the 64KiB read buffer, the single-open gate+fold, the lazy mtime) — the port adds only the SESSION_SCAN_MAX_CACHED_STATES=4096 state cap (files with no usage records never trip the usage budget). (2) CHARACTERIZATION (leg 1): the many-session fixture built FROM THE REAL ONE (the bench repo's session-imageheavy-vizbuilder.jsonl, 22.9MB/6,870 rows/1,792 assistant-usage entries, sha f6ab958a80bc1c37...): N byte-identical copies per tier with a unique same-shape id in line 1 (deterministic sha256-derived ids, byte count preserved) and distinct mtimes (deterministic newest-first order); tiers {1,10,50,100,250} + the boundary pair {223,224}; a per-tier sha256 manifest. One lane-private Prime VM (rsqkejooqyhh3oexkwa9kb0v, ubuntu:22.04, 16c/32GB/120GB, rustup 1.98.1, the pinned tip fda40b56a, origin/rust moved to a8ebf4c64 during the campaign — the lane pins fda40b56a). The probe: an untracked pa-daemon example (roster_manyfile_probe.rs, binary sha 959a4be303bd1c535a5a5c050a2d13cc193f69fedad91eb01a34ca6af3a32607) with three arms — scan (list_sessions per pass; pass 0 = cold: empty scan-state, warm page cache; passes 1-6 warm), meta (the scan's metadata pass alone: readdir + per-file stat + sort), folds (per-file read_session_info in metadata order) — each printing rows + a sha256 row oracle over the canonical row serialization in scan order. 5 fresh-process scan slots + 2 decomp slots per tier; noop CPU calibration + loadavg at every slot; the fleet I/O advisory v1.0 probe pair at the pre/mid/post leg boundaries (>=40 isolated fresh 4KB write+fsync+rename @0.5s spacing + >=20 repeat-fsync; host-relative labels; NO-CEILING labeling); a page-cache-cold confirm leg (sync + drop_caches per trial, tier 10) run as its own regime; a gateless pilot campaign (kept as the reproducibility check). (3) THE CUT DECISION (leg 3): the measured slope + the cliff decide; the divergence cases route to the operator BEFORE any implementation (the parent's directive: the divergence decision is a product call).
parity_notes: MEASUREMENT-ONLY LANE: no product change, no PR, the probe tree never ships (an untracked example, env-gated nothing — a standalone binary). THE TS-PARITY FINDINGS (the anchors): (a) TS RE-SCANS per cold process — the roster is built by folding every session file on the first catalog touch of each fresh daemon; the ONLY cache is the in-memory sessionScanStates Map inside the catalog child process (which dies with the daemon); there is NO persistent on-disk index in TS, so a cross-process row cache/index would be an INTERNAL-BEHAVIOR DIVERGENCE requiring the TS-parity case + a row-identity oracle + the operator's (Kevin's) sign-off BEFORE implementation. (b) THE 400k RETAINED-USAGE-ENTRY BUDGET IS A SHARED TS+PORT DESIGN POINT, not a port artifact: TS session-manager.ts line 1340 (SESSION_SCAN_MAX_RETAINED_USAGE_ENTRIES = 400_000) with insertion-order (oldest-first) eviction in storeSessionScanState — the port mirrors both (info.rs: SESSION_SCAN_MAX_RETAINED_USAGE_ENTRIES = 400_000 + the LRU BTreeMap front eviction). The design comment's point (~2k sessions / ~75 usage entries per session) is EXCEEDED by the real-session class measured here (1,792 entries per file): the cliff sits at 224 such sessions in BOTH runtimes — TS would thrash identically (its walk is readdir-cyclic, ours mtime-cyclic; the cyclic-LRU-over-capacity 100%-miss mechanism is order-agnostic). (c) The row oracle: every pass, slot, and arm produced the IDENTICAL sha256 row oracle per tier (scan == folds == warm == cold == pilot == campaign == page-cache-cold) — the thrash costs time, never correctness (the rows are byte-identical to the fresh fold's). (d) The port's fold is already the fast side of the pair (the #2919 borrow machinery + the single-open + the 64KiB buffer); the per-byte parse floor is the dominant cost (the catalog-stats census's class).

measurements.cold_curve_fit: linear in N at the real-session unit: ~9.9-10.3ms per 22.9MB session (~0.44ms/MB); R²~1 over the tiers; the metadata pass is negligible (0.010ms at 1 file -> 0.254ms at 250) and the fold is the whole cost (folds == scan within noise)
measurements.warm_cliff: the scan-state cache serves ~free warm scans (0.006ms at 1 -> 0.627ms at 100 files) until the retained-usage-entry budget trips: the predicted cliff at ceil(400_000/1,792) = 224 files landed EXACTLY (tier 223: warm p50 1.502ms, no thrash; tier 224: warm p50 2,189.9ms == cold — the cyclic walk over a capacity-223 cache is a 100% miss EVERY pass; tier 250: warm p50 2,468.6ms == cold 2,481.6ms)
measurements.page_cache_cold: drop_caches per trial at tier 10: 106.5/107.7ms vs the warm-cache cold 100.7ms — no measurable change (the class matches the imageheavy record's finding; the fold is CPU-parse-bound)

validity_notes: (1) ORACLE: the sha256 row oracle is identical across every pass (cold + 6 warm), every slot (5/tier), every arm (scan == folds), both campaigns (pilot gateless + gated), the boundary tiers, and the page-cache-cold leg — the rows are byte-stable under every regime measured. (2) REPRODUCIBILITY: the pilot-vs-campaign cold p50 deltas are +1.0/+1.7/+1.6/-0.1/+0.7% at tiers 1/10/50/100/250. (3) CALIBRATION: the noop CPU loop p50 0.063s (min 0.060/max 0.066 over 27 slots), loadavg1 p50 0.40 max 0.76 — the CPU class healthy and stable throughout. (4) IO ADVISORY v1.0: the flush class was DEGRADED-UNIFORM across every gate (fresh write+fsync+rename p50 83-89ms, rate20=100%, max up to 206ms; repeat-fsync p50 0.2ms with one >50ms outlier per window) — a HOST-regime state, uniform pre/mid/post, labeled on every leg per the phase model; the measurement legs are CACHED READS, unaffected by the flush class (the precedent + the drop_caches leg's null result + the noop calib all confirm); no absolute ceiling was assumed anywhere (NO-CEILING: the fresh-class max 206ms at mid_after_tier_250 is regime evidence, labeled, not excluded). (5) CROSS-TIER comparability: every tier is the SAME unit file (byte-identical except line 1's id, byte count preserved) on the SAME VM and binary; the only variables are N and the tier's directory. (6) The warm-thrash finding is a MECHANISM-verified cliff: the boundary pair (223 vs 224) matches the budget arithmetic exactly (223x1,792=399,616 <= 400,000; 224x1,792=401,408 > 400,000); the state-count cap (4,096) is not in play (250 << 4,096). (7) The page-cache-cold leg is a separate regime, labeled as such (its purpose is the fold-cost attribution, not the curve). (8) The fixture ids/mtimes are deterministic (sha256-derived), so the fixtures are byte-reproducible from the bench repo's real fixture + the archived builder. (9) The probe's folds arm calls read_session_info (the fold without the scan's gate); its oracle equals the scan oracle on every tier (the shared-open gate path adds no row variance).
outcome: THE CHARACTERIZATION (the open question, answered): the cold roster scan scales LINEARLY with session count at the real-session unit — ~10ms per 22.9MB session per cold scan (100 real sessions ~1.0s; 250 ~2.5s; 500 extrapolates ~5s) — and the warm path COLLAPSES past 224 such sessions: the scan-state cache's 400k retained-usage-entry budget + the cyclic LRU walk turns EVERY catalog touch into a full re-fold for the daemon's lifetime (warm == cold measured at 224 and 250). THE COST IS THE FOLD (the metadata pass is 0.01% of it; the per-file overhead ~0.01ms; the per-byte parse floor dominates). THE PARITY ANSWER (leg 2): TS re-scans per cold process with an in-memory-only resume cache; NO on-disk index exists in TS; the 400k budget + the insertion-order eviction are TS's own (session-manager.ts:1340-1387) — the cliff is a SHARED design point exceeded (TS's ~2k-session/~75-entry design point vs the real class's 1,792 entries/file), so BOTH runtimes lose the cache on exactly the many-session box the task asks about. THE CUT LANDSCAPE (leg 3, NOT implemented — divergence-grade, routed to the operator per the parent's directive): (a) a cross-boot persistent row index would cut the cold-boot wall (250-box: 2.5s -> index-read+stats ~50-200ms; the index would hold the folded rows keyed by the generation identity — ~16MB at the 250 class since the real session's search corpus sits at the 64KiB cap) — the LARGEST divergence (TS has nothing like it; TS ignores a non-.jsonl index file in the sessions dir, so cross-runtime compat is safe; needs the row-identity oracle + a served-path assertion + the degradation oracles); (b) the scan-state budget policy (the cliff fix): raise the budget (memory-bound tradeoff: the maps are ~1792 entries/file) or a light row-state tier for unchanged files (drops the usage-map accounting; grown files re-fold whole instead of resuming — a warm-path tradeoff) — a smaller but real TS divergence (TS keeps the map + the resume); (c) per-byte fold cuts — already mined by #2919 (-7%), the parse floor dominates, diminishing. The honest negative does NOT apply: the cost class is NOT bounded (the curve + the cliff).
